Artists.bio: Bradley Theodore is a visual artist. Born in the Turks and Caicos Islands, he now resides in New York City. Theodore gained prominence as an artist through the popularity of a street art murals of fashion icons Anna Wintour and Karl Lagerfeld.

Iman Omari is an American singer, record producer and DJ from Los Angeles, California. Beginning as a producer for artists such as Kendrick Lamar and OverDoz., Omari was convinced to become his own artist by friends. He released his debut album, Energy, in 2011, which received positive reviews.

Bliss Lau’s approach is centered around the idea that jewelry is a physical experience, one that is inspired by sensuality and structure. Through this ideology and the combination of her Chinese and American culture, she has evolved her collection from leather goods to the trademark fine, body, and semi-fine jewelry of today.

Tripp Derrick Barnes is a South Carolina-born, New York City-based multimedia artist working at the intersection of Art, Entertainment and Technology.Tripp’s Pop Art portraits are an act of recognition and preservation along with escapism, placing his subjects in a sort of alternate world.

Shochan (Sho Ishikura) is a Soul Singer who writes and produces his own music. Son of an American mother and a Japanese father, his parents met in Japan while his mother was teaching abroad. From a young age he displayed dedication as a self-styled artist, following in the footsteps of his mother, a working painter.

1st generation American artist infused with a Caribbean, Asian and Irish heritage. Being homeless before he built his art inspired by his life experience in the streets of Papine to Copenhagen. Ptah comes to Ishikawa to present a unique performance piece to provoke thoughts on a concept exploring worth in terms of cultural and artistic exchange.

Rachel Schultz is a New York-based artist and Creative Associate at Idun. Rachel's art work spans various subject matters but most often explores the human psyche. She is interested in juxtaposing color and subject matter, like that of anxiety and mental health, which can be veiled, dark and elusive with a lighter, more buoyant palette.

I'am a contemporary artist I enjoy textures, geometric shapes, jolted lines and deep rich colors. My visual rhythmic cadence sets the stage for the expression of personal thoughts that all must confront. It invites my audience to enter a personal conversation of reflection and confession.

Matheus is greatly influenced by the city he now calls home -- New York has long been the epicenter of fashion, hip hop, and street art, where he feels his interest in contemporary art, architecture, and interior design has grown exponentially.

Born in Boston, Massachusetts, TRIHUMPH began painting with stencils at 15 before leaving school at 17 pursue art professionally. Now based in Brooklyn, New York, TRIHUMPH has since exhibited his works in galleries around the world. Basing his creative explorations in the unpredictable essence of scribbling, TRIHUMPH paints with plasticity and a spirit of adventure.

Franco’s work manifests itself in a variety of mediums, all intended to express the cycles of nature and what he calls “the flat circularity of time.” Franco’s “Driftwood” series “is an intervened extension of a journey”. The wood that has traveled from faraway lands, like Africa, that by happenstance ends up on a beach in Long Island, artificially “blends” in an extended expression, a final suggestion of the influence of man.

Alessandra's pieces articulate, like nymphets from a mobile garden by meansof space. The artist shows a succession of simultaneous occurrences, which may be understood as the negative and the positive. The artist plays with these, erasing, isolating and/or dissolving the parts while still maintaining their identifiably due to the representation of margins.

My desire is to express mystery and beauty through art while awaking recognition of those qualities in the viewer. The painting then becomes a mirror that awakens the artist and the viewer while transporting each beyond the boundaries of politics, culture, and religion. Gilewicz has learned that, through his art, he can share with the viewer his appreciation of beauty, mystery, and harmony.

By cutting snippets of tape with a razor blade, adding them to Plexiglas and lacquering a half-inch hardening glaze of poly-urethane for a stained glass effect.He erected a host house called the Chocolate Factory, a 20,000 sq. ft loft that hosted 550 people in its time and was the chosen locale for the Justina Valentine ft. Fetty Wap music video.

Patrick Smith is a realist painter who defies conventional standard of beauty, gender and sexuality.  His method consists of a maniacal, layered, detailed obsessed, chiaroscuro technique. Because of the ambiguous quality of its surface, paper is his canvas of choice, giving the viewer the illusion of staring at a photograph at a first glance.

Charlotte Hall Dos Santos is a Brazilian-Norwegian jazz singer, composer, and arranger, currently based in Berlin. Her music mixes South-American traditions, jazz, neo soul, and tasty beats, with music history samples in a colorful way. Dos Santos released her debut solo album Cleo in 2017 on the label Fresh Selects.

Nancy XiáoRong Valentine is a self-taught multi-disciplinary artist from Fergus Falls, Minnesota. Drawing technical inspiration from her Chinese heritage, Nancy strives to reveal hidden connections to her audience through implied design. Many of her works communicate an affinity and appreciation for the simplistic, the natural and the feminine form; her themes often revolve around the connection point of the natural and the spiritual.

Mike Larry Draw is combination of Hip Hop/Rock/Soul has created a positive movement in music that influences. He is a Polymath; and his unique approach combines cross genre sounds with an artistic vision that cultivates into a noteworthy media experiences.

Jayden Pyram is a generation-z  influencer, widely recognized for his widely recognized children’s modeling campaigns with major fashion labels from film to print. Jayden now sets his sights on conquering the music industry and fashion industry on an international scale with creative developments in London and Japan.

Melanie Charles is a Brooklyn-born singer-songwriter, actress, and flutist of Haitian descent, with a creative fluidity spanning jazz, soul, experimental, and Haitian roots music. Charles latest release “The Girl with the Green shoes” established Charles as a progressive voice in Jazz catching the attention of India Arie and a feature in The New York Times Sunday routine, as well as The Village Voice. You can hear her collaging her musical DNA into jazz-studded multi-instrumentalism and dipping a toe into the experimental... there's an uncanny cohesion to Charles' music." - Village Voice

Charles graduated from the New School for Jazz and Contemporary Music with a BFA in vocal jazz performance and trained under the tutelage of jazz masters Reggie Workman, Charles Tolliver, Junior Mance, Janet Lawson, Carla Cook, and Billy Harper, has worked with Herlin Riley, Ellis Marsalis, Pedrito Martinez, ELEW, Jean Grae, SZA, and the Gorillaz. Her recent television appearances include Good Morning America, SNL, and The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.

Under the moniker D’flower,a new experience has been born using Roland SPs, loop pedals, and the flute to create a Chaka Khan meets Badu-esque “sonic collage “ fusing RnB, jazz, samples and Haitian folk songs. This project aims to blur the lines between social classes, cultures, genders, genres, and theories to create a world where opposing elements can co-exist.

Half Japanese, half New Zealander musician Mark de Clive-Lowe has called LA home for the past 10 years. Equal parts composer, jazz musician, found-sound remixer and club music producer, de Clive-Lowe tours his multi-faceted live show in both solo and band configurations internationally. He has released over a dozen albums and hundreds of collaborations and remixes creating with musicians, artists and DJs from all around the world and across a broad range of genres. De Clive-Lowe has been featured artist at numerous festivals since his international recording debut in 2000 including Yerba Buena Centre for the Arts, SF Jazz, Montreal Jazz Festival, Grand Performances, Lincoln Center, North Sea Jazz Festival, Tokyo Crossover Jazz Festival, Capetown Jazz Festival. His critically acclaimed club night CHURCH, which he describes as a mash up of jazz club, live remix experiment and dance party, has seen him on stage with multiple generations of the world’s most respected jazz, soul and hip hop artists, and his latest project HERITAGE sees him making a deep dive into his own Japanese roots, interpreting it through the lens of jazz and electronica.

(the) avant-garde soulful Pianist/DJ/Producer delivers his lifetime of journeys to different musical ports in a concise package, seamlessly... transporting not just in genre but in emotion and spirit. - HuffingtonPost

Mange Hellberg is a multi-discipline artist from Sweden. Mange's work reflects his childhood experiences with his father, using painting and singing as an outlet to communicate the hardships of their relationship.

Since 2015 manges has painted everyday, with a series of exibitions in Sweden, Norway and New York, after experiencing life homeless and afflicted by drugs and alcohol. Prior to Mange's visual arts exploration, Mange released an album of work as a musician in 2012, topping the Spotify charts in Sweden with millions of streams.

Mange has partnered with celebrity actor Peter Stormare, and Tattoo artist Oscar Åkermo to launch an arts and music foundation for kids experiencing troubles with sex and violence abuse.

Kaira Widodo is a rising Indonesian Muslim American photographer based in Hoboken, New Jersey and raised in New York City. She is currently studying at the School Of Visual Arts taking a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Photography and Video.

Following the steps of her family; both visual artists, Kaira found a passion for the arts as well. Born in America and raised in Indonesia for 4 years, Kaira seeks time as a missing period if it not captured. She believes that if we do not capture every moment of time, it would not exist. Kaira's work is identified as a photojournalistic approach that describes culture and identity through the environment and traditions of the street or personal life. She pursues her work as a collection of photographs that resemble a life that once was or could have never happened. Kaira works with mixed media such as photography mainly analog and solar powered photography. She creates a variety in media such as creating a short video that shares the same themes as her photography.

Her recent video work, 'Duplicity' is based on her own personal life and the confusion of being raised as a Muslim American. It shares both ends of the of who she is as a Muslim and who she is as an American. It explains further if the impact of being a Muslim in America has increased or decreased the view of her own religion.

Hiten Bawa is an artist, architect and Accessibility Consultant based in Johannesburg, South Africa. Hiten is a profoundly deaf person with bilateral cochlear implants. He works primarily with acrylic paints, watercolours and inks to express his cultural identity and perspectives of people with disabilities. Bawa's artwork overlaps his interest in the South African Indian diaspora and South Africa's Apartheid based architectural structures which manipulate access as a medium of control. Bawa also goes on to parallel the hand signals of sign language with Classical Indian Dance hand movements and local taxi hand directions in a creole styled visual language from his unique perspective.

He holds a Master of Architecture (Prof) degree from the University of Cape Town and runs his own creative practice called Studio HB. He is currently working on designing barrier-free environments for people with disabilities across housing, transportation, interior design, urban design and landscape design. Bawa was a finalist for the inaugural SA TAXI Foundation Art Award in 2015 and is a part of the J.P. Morgan Chase Art Collection.

Whitney (b. 1993, Brooklyn) lives and works in Brooklyn, NYC. Being a New York native made the art world easily accessible, enabling exploration within the ever-present diversity and vibrant culture of the city. After being awarded scholarships to attend the Fine Art Intensive programs at New York University and Pratt College, Whitney received her Bachelor’s of Fine Arts with a minor in Art History from the Fashion Institute of Technology. Now Whitney works as a Mixed Media Artist, using both mediums of painting and printmaking in her works that investigate notions of identity - “who or what a person or thing is”. Whitney's works are an expressive experience employing heavy brush strokes that gives texture and movement in each work. With great admiration, Whitney has become heavily influenced by numerous artists, in particular Schiele, Saville, Marden and Walker.

Le Poodle is a singer-songwriter, producer, creative director, visual artist, and doctor based in Miami, FL. Her main focus is combining her knowledge of the arts and sciences in order to address social issues while working with or inspiring others to do the same. To her, art is synonymous with social movement.

Yazmine Graham is born and raised in Newark New Jersey. Graham is an alumni of Arts High School where she attended as an Visual Arts major and is current working as a Teaching-Artist for GlassRoots Inc; a non for profit glass arts studio. She is also a full-time student of the Michael Graves College School of Public Architecture at Kean University. Grahams work is peppered with lots of color and takes on the various forms of weird, vulnerable, playful and sometimes political aspects of American cultures. In a similar way, fashion and music references are layered throughout Graham's work as she challenges herself to pair daydreams and visuals from some of her favorite experiences, people and visual artist along with materials like marker, watercolor and acrylic paint, or glass to create beautiful visuals. With Graham's work she hopes to provoke adventure where inspiration has faded, begin journeys by acknowledging existing life and the understanding that every moment should start with a tabula rasa.

Besmira desires for her work to communicate to audiences that there are things that everyone sees, but there are also things people pretend they don't see. I explore not only why that is but how long can it last. How long can someone be presented with such raw truths and emotions and just blatantly reject them? Besmira looks to this phenomenon in reference to the identity of a person and aims to convey the deeper meanings behind people's eyes, and what they wish everyone could see.

Kaira Villanueva explores boundaries between science fiction narratives and natural phenomena in oil and digital paintings. Her work in engineering strongly influences her paintings, often depicting themes that push the limitations of current scientific progress. Majority of her pieces implement a combination of negative space and tonalism that grounds the central theme of Auribus teneo lupum. Her art opens up the anxiety that exists in the liminal state between the present and the future.

Kayla Vasquez is photographer born and raised in New York City. Kayla often travels to places like Pennsylvania and Florida, USA to capture landscapes. Kayla recently finished her first year at the School of Visual Arts which has greatly helped assisted in the development of her photography style and progression. I mostly work with digital photography but my roots with photography start with analog photography. Before attending SVA, Kayla studied black and white photography. Although most of my new work is dominated by digital, film will always be my favorite form of photography.

Skylar Davis, is a multi discipline artist living in Louisville, KY. Growing up in a fundamentalist Christian majority small town in Kentucky, Skylar was raised to be a lady and remain pure until marriage in order to be seen as a holier person. It wasn’t until she was older, that she 'saw the light” and realized just be yourself and embrace your desires. Feeling herself is Skylar's playful response.

Chuck was raised in San Francisco CA and is the Artistic Director/Choreographer of bicoastal dance company, UNA - creating work in NYC and San Francisco. Chuck holds a BFA in dance from NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts and am also a certified GYROTONIC® teacher.

As Artistic Director/Choreographer of UNA, Chuck investigates ways to increase people-to-people connections while illuminating the diversity of human experience. Chuck is interested in how topics of gender, identity and unity can be involved in dance and dance film, transforming the way we can experience ourselves and our connection to others.


In 2017 Chuck was a selected choreographic fellow for the Alvin Ailey Dance Foundation New Directions Choreography Lab made possible by generous support from the Ford Foundation. I was an Artist in Residence at the 92nd St. Y’s Harkness Dance Center (2018-2019) and in the coming year will be a CUNY artist in residence at Brooklyn College (2019-2020). He was also a selected Dance Initiative Artist In Residence in Carbondale Colorado (2018) the recipient of the Rainin Opportunity Fund, premiering his evening-length work COLORING at and in association with the ODC Theater (San Francisco, 2019). I have taught technique, improvisation and set repertory for the NYU Tisch Summer High School Program (2017-2019). Along with UNA company members, I have taught at Malashock Dance, Dance PAW, Velocity Dance Center, Gibney Dance Center, Lowell High School, ODC Dance Commons, SF Arts Institute, LAB Sessions/IATI Studios and Booker T. Washington High School for Performing and Visual Arts. Additionally, the company has done outreach in NYC including lec-dems and workshops with Williamsburg Charter, Brooklyn International, Beacon High Schools and the Professional Performing Arts School. My dance training includes studying at the San Francisco Ballet School, ODC, LINES Ballet, SEAD in Austria, American Dance Festival, Jacob's Pillow Contemporary Program and Springboard Dance Montreal. I have studied Ohad Naharin's movement language, Gaga, in San Francisco, NYC, Montreal and Israel and attended Hofesh Shechter's Professional Intensive in London. I have had the pleasure of performing professionally for companies and artists such as Jérôme Bel's The Show Must Go On at the Joyce, Martin Løfsnes/360° Dance Company, Rebecca Margolick/Maxx Berkowitz's birds sing a pretty song in NYC, Vancouver, Sofia, Jerusalem and San Diego, From the Horse's Mouth, MADBOOTS DANCE at the Jacob's Pillow Festival and in Vancouver, Zoe|Juniper, Katharine Hawthorne, Danaka Dance, GroundWorks DanceTheater performing the work of Noa Zuk, as well as Chihiro Shimizu and Artists among others. I was the recipient of the Homer Avila Award and the Jacob’s Pillow School Professional Advancement Award.

I grew up in San Diego, CA and moved to NYC in 2011 to pursue Dance and Psychology at NYU. I have been living here since graduating in 2015. I am a freelance professional dancer, certified and practicing yoga teacher, and visual artist currently residing in Brooklyn, NY. I received a BA in Psychology and a BFA in Dance from NYU, with additional training at the Salzburg Experimental Academy of Dance. I have been performing and collaborating for Chuck Wilt's Company, UNA, since 2015 - and have been a Rehearsal Assistant for the company since 2017.  I have been a company member with Helen Simoneau Danse since January 2018 and previously danced with the Stephen Petronio Company from 2015-2017. With the Stephen Petronio Company I performed nationally and in Slovakia, Croatia, Bulgaria, Thailand, Vietnam, and Singapore. While in Southeast Asia, through the historic Dance Motion USA organization, I was a part of many teaching experiences with disabled populations. I have also assisted dance classes for the blind at the Lighthouse Guild in NYC.

Andres Alvarez is a self-taught visual artist born in the Dominican Republic. He moved at the age of 13 to live in Puerto Rico, and then made a move to NYC at the age of 18, where he still resides.

He had manifested his artistic abilities through drawing since a very early age, but it wasn’t until 2013 that he decided to further develop his technical skills and expand his range as an artist by exploring and learning about the techniques used by the old masters, such as Bouguereau, Alma-Tadema, Diego Velazquez, etc., and some of his modern-day art heroes, such as Frank Frazetta, Cesar Santos, Donato Giancola, Jeremy Mann, Simon Bizley, and others.

His early work began as a rediscovery of himself as an artist and a still ongoing search for his place in the visual art spectrum. As a result, this search highlighted a passion for portraiture work through the use of oil paint on canvas but also has a constant need to capture various subjects and elements that are the makeup of his interests and sparks of curiosity.

As Andres grows as an artist, so does the physical scale of his pieces, which drove him to inevitably seek out mural artwork, a field that he is looking to further develop as part of his repertoire of services as a professional artist, which already includes portrait commissions, the sale of original art, digital art direction and graphic design.

His goal is to be able to help people get in touch with their higher selves through the art experience, and enjoy the art journey as much as possible.

Featured in the Chicago Design Museum, SCAD Permanent Collection and several self-hosted shows, “Sirsu” is a mixed media artist who works with portraits, physical objects and digital works in abstract...or at least feels more abstracted than organic. Borrowing heavily from the works of Jason Thielke and Ashley Wood, Sirsu looks to evoke emotion through dynamic lines and raw energy with compositions that look ethereal and light.

George F. Baker III is an Atlanta-based Muralist, Illustrator, and Public Speaker who infuses a child-like joy into all of his creative endeavors. Over the course of 6 years practicing muralism, he has painted over 50 murals across the United States (as well as a couple in London) and has produced numerous illustrations. Regardless of the medium, he is always eager to offer encouragement to individuals, urging them to embrace their inner-child more in their daily lives. He firmly believes that by doing so, people become the most authentic versions of themselves.

"I use my art to express who I am, how I think, and what my personal experience is. I grew up in a very small town and felt very different from everyone around me, so I've used my art to comfort me and explores how my mind works."

Matthew Loyd is an artist specializing in illustration and design. Alongside his creative pursuits, he is the founder of 20XX Magazine, an art and culture publication. His work spans print and digital media, showcasing his talent in oil pastel, marker, and pen and pencil drawings. Inspired by comic books and manga, his art features captivating narratives and original characters. Currently, he's exploring acrylic painting on MTA MetroCards, aiming to create a unique body of work.

Sarah was born and raised in Miami, she graduated with a dean's award from the Visual Art department of New world school of the Arts in 2013. After high school she graduated from the Kansas City Art Institute majoring in Ceramics and completed a certificate program focused on Asian art. Through the influence of the certificate program, after graduating in 2017 Sarah was accepted into the JET program to move and start a life in Japan. Through the JET program Sarah had the opportunity to work in a high school in Amami Ōshima (奄美大島), Japan. While working a full time job as an English teacher and volunteering as an assistant in the school's art club she also began an apprenticeship in the ceramic studio, Yachaboyaki (野茶坊焼). She studied under the ceramic master Junichi Ikenomi (池波陶柳) for three years becoming his first and last apprentice.  Since returning to the US in 2020 Sarah has continued actively making art and became a founding member of 2win! Studio in 2021.

Miami born artist Samantha Noelia Ferrer uses her Cuban roots to make a variety of work. She is a current graduate of the Kansas City Art Institute receiving a BFA in Ceramics with a minor in Asian Studies. Samantha has worked with local and international artists through internships and has interest working abroad. Her interest in Asian art and ceramics is used as a stylistic influence within her work.

Marie is an artist based in Atlanta, GA. With an eclectic background in production and geology, she’s built innovation programs for R/GA, Comcast, REI, and UConn; working with all kinds of startups from outdoor retail to climate tech. She’s on a journey from corporate girlie to freelance explorer, currently deep diving into her artistic interests in photography, pottery, and nail art.

Washington D.C.-born and New York-based artist KAMAUU, a multifaceted talent as a rapper, poet, and thinker, intertwines his higher calling of service with his creative expressions, believing deeply in contributing to something greater than oneself. Influenced by a childhood rich with diverse musical and artistic exposures, thanks to his parents, KAMAUU's journey in music began from an early age, leading to his significant debut on No Wyld's "QUEEN" and subsequent successes with singles like "Jusfayu" and his own EPs and albums. His music, a blend of rap, reggae, soul, and more, serves as a platform for growth and introspection, encapsulated in his latest project, "TheKAMAUU-CASSETTE: MíXD GRēēNS," which symbolizes his fertile and burgeoning creativity. Through his work, KAMAUU aims to inspire growth and resilience, sharing his journey not as a teacher but as a fellow traveler in the art of living and serving.

Logan Martinez is a multidisciplinary artist whose talents flourish in the realms of novel writing, illustrating, and macramé jewelry design. With a profound ability to breathe life into stories, Logan weaves narratives not just through captivating prose but also through expressive brush strokes and intricate threads. At the heart of Logan's artistic expression is a vibrant, nature-inspired passion, fueling a creative journey that transcends mediums to evoke the vivid tapestry of the natural world.

Javon Angela, a visual artist from Nashville, Tennessee, crafts artwork that weaves together complex details with a spectrum of colors. For Javon, creating art is a deeply reflective process, serving as a channel for tranquility that imbues her pieces with a calming influence.

Dillon McCraw is a digitally native graphic artist renowned for his dynamic storytelling and intricate worldbuilding. His artistic style is ever-evolving, seamlessly oscillating between realistic illustration and contemporary iconography, making each of his creations a unique exploration of visual narrative.

Miguel Flores, originally from the slums of Ecuador, found his early years marked by the country's financial crisis before moving to New Jersey. His art, deeply rooted in the human condition, navigates the complex interplay between realistic and abstract portrayals of people, set against the backdrop of contemporary societal issues and future anxieties. Flores' distinctive backgrounds are abstract impressionist collages, weaving together elements like newspaper headlines, scientific papers, and mixed media to reflect the chaotic tapestry of modern life. Working primarily with acrylic layers before adding oil paint, Miguel is now exploring the integration of electronic waste into his paintings and employing "collaborative intelligence" to democratize the creative process via social media, inviting a global community to shape his art

About.EN:
FUSION is an International Artists Residency platform that partners with private institutions in Japan to develop and present impactful experiences to artists worldwide. The FUSION residency's merge a select group of artists that vary in discipline,experience, and background per program. Through an intense two weeks explorative and productive open schedule, artists are immersed into the hosting residence and local community.

FUSION is the product of an ever growing desire to bridge global cultural gaps. We believe in a universal language that speaks through the arts, and aim to share that language wherever we can.
About.JP: FUSION は、日本の民間機関とパートナーシップを組み、世界中のアーティストにインパクトのある体験を提供する国際アーティストレジデンシープラットフォームです。 FUSION レジデンシーでは、異なる専門分野、経験、背景を持つ選ばれたアーティストのグループを各プログラムごとにおいて融合し、2 週間の生産的で探求的なスケジュールの中で、アーティストは滞在先とその土地の地域コミュニティに溶け込みます。 FUSIONは、世界的な文化のギャップを埋めたいという強い想いから成り立つものであり、私たちはアートを通して語られる普遍的な言語を信じ、その言語をできる限り共有していくことを目指しています。

Artists.EN:
Fusion artists are select creators and organizers from diverse backgrounds and disciplines, driven by a common desire to transcend the limitations that often divide us.

Our shared bond is rooted in a deep appreciation for unconventional exploration within our creative domains. Collectively, we resonate with the profound impact that change can bring to our lives, and we actively seek ways to harness its potential.

Within the serene and rural creative zones of Japan, we find solace away from the relentless pace of mainstream life. It is in these unique surroundings that we discover the space and stillness necessary to nurture our creative aspirations and push the boundaries of our craft.
Artists.JP:
Fusionアーティストは、私たちを分断し制限するものを超えたいという共通の願いを持ち、多様なバックグラウンドを持つ、多分野から選ばれたクリエイターやオーガナイザーたちです。

その中で共有された絆とは、それぞれのクリエイティブな領域においての型破りな探求心への深い感謝の気持ちに根ざしています。変化が人生にもたらす深い影響に共鳴し、私たちはその可能性を活用する方法を積極的に模索しています。

激流のような速さで進むメインストリームの生活から離れ、日本の静かな田舎の創造的な空間で安らぎを見出し、こうした独特の環境の中で創造に対する野心を育み、技術の限界を超えるために必要な空間と静寂を見つけ出すのです。

Eiheiji.EN: The Fusion Residency culminates with a visit to Eiheiji Temple, a well-known Zen Buddhist temple. This serene sanctuary, nestled amidst lush forests, encourages contemplation and meditation. The temple's architecture and surroundings evoke a sense of timelessness, offering a profound opportunity for reflection and inspiration.
Eiheiji.JP: Fusion Residencyの締めくくりとして、参加者は有名な禅寺である永平寺を訪れます。この静寂に包まれた聖域は、豊かな森林に囲まれ、瞑想と内省を促します。寺院の建築やその周辺の自然は、時を超えた感覚を呼び起こし、深い内省やインスピレーションの機会を提供します。

Journey.EN:
The flagship Fusion Residency program 'Fusion Kaga' journeys through Tokyo, Kaga, Kanazawa, Komatsu, and Eiheiji is a dynamic exploration of Japan's contrasting facets, from the energetic urban pulse of Tokyo to the tranquil and culturally rich landscapes of Ishikawa. Each location holds its unique allure, shaping the artists' experiences and fostering transformation and creativity throughout their residency.

The journey, like the Shinkansen ride, is a transition from one world to another, leaving participants with lasting memories and inspiration drawn from the tapestry of Japan's art, culture, and tradition
Journey.JP:
Fusion Residencyの旅は、東京、加賀、金沢、小松、永平寺を通して、日本の対照的な側面を探求するものです。東京のエネルギッシュな都市の鼓動から、石川県の静寂で文化的に豊かな風景まで、各地が独自の魅力を持ち、アーティストたちの経験を形作り、滞在中の変容と創造性を促します。

その旅は、まるで新幹線のライドのように、一つの世界から別の世界へと移行します。日本のアート、文化、伝統の織りなす世界から得た忘れがたい思い出とインスピレーションは参加者の心に残り続けます。

Kaga City.EN: Kaga, the heart of the Fusion Residency experience, welcomes artists with open arms. This city is renowned for its onsen (hot springs) culture, which provides a unique opportunity for relaxation and reflection. Artists settle into traditional Japanese accommodations with tatami-matted rooms, immersing themselves in the local culture. Kaga's streets are adorned with artisanal shops, reflecting its rich tradition of craftsmanship.
Kaga City.JP: Fusion Residencyの中心である加賀は、アーティストたちを温かく迎え入れてくれます。この街は、休息と内省という特別な機会を与えてくれる温泉文化で有名です。アーティストたちは畳敷きの和室がある伝統的な日本の宿泊施設に身を落ち着け、地元文化に浸ります。加賀の街並みには職人の店が並び、豊かな工芸の伝統が反映されています。

Kanazawa.EN:
Kanazawa, a neighboring city to Kaga, is home to the 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, making it a hub for artistic inspiration. This city, often referred to as 'Little Kyoto' due to its preserved Edo-era architecture and well-maintained geisha districts, beckons with its rich cultural heritage. Artists explore its gardens, including the renowned Kenrokuen Garden, a masterpiece of Japanese landscaping.

The city's craft traditions thrive, with gold leaf production being a notable specialty. Visiting workshops and galleries provides a glimpse into these time-honored crafts. The fusion of tradition and innovation in Kanazawa mirrors the artistic journey itself.
Kanazawa.JP:
加賀に隣接する金沢には21世紀美術館などがあり、芸術的インスピレーションの中心地となっています。この街は、保存された江戸時代の建築や手入れの行き届いた芸者地区があることなどから「小京都」とも呼ばれ、その豊かな文化遺産が魅力です。アーティストたちは、名園として知られる兼六園を含む庭園を探求し、日本の造園の傑作を堪能します。

この街の工芸の伝統は息づいており、特に金箔の生産が有名で、ワークショップやギャラリーを訪れることで、これらの伝統的な工芸に触れることができます。金沢における伝統とイノベーションの融合は、アーティストたちの芸術的な旅そのものを映し出しています。

Shinkansen.EN: The Shinkansen, Japan's iconic high-speed train system, becomes the conduit for transitioning from Tokyo's urban hustle to the rural landscapes of Ishikawa. The sleek, futuristic trains whisk passengers away at incredible speeds, affording them breathtaking views of Japan's changing scenery. This journey is not just about distance but also a transition from the urban chaos to the tranquility of the countryside, setting the stage for the artistic exploration that awaits.
Shinkansen.JP: 新幹線、日本のアイコニックな高速鉄道システムは、東京の都市の喧騒から石川県の田園風景へと移行するための架け橋となります。流線型で未来的なデザインの列車は、驚異的なスピードで乗客を運び、日本の変わりゆく息をのむような景色を楽しませてくれます。この旅は単なる距離の移動ではなく、都市の混沌から田舎の静けさへの移行でもあり、これより待ち受けている芸術探求や冒険というステージへ向けての準備段階とも言えるでしょう。

Tokyo.EN:
Tokyo, the bustling metropolis and the starting point of the Fusion Residency journey, serves as a vibrant prelude to the artistic adventure awaiting participants. This sprawling city, known for its skyscrapers and neon lights, is a vibrant fusion of modernity and tradition. Artists from around the world gather here, exploring Tokyo's fast-paced energy before embarking on their creative voyage.

Tokyo offers a kaleidoscope of experiences, from the serene gardens of the Imperial Palace to the lively streets of Harajuku, where fashionistas and trendsetters congregate. The city's culinary scene is a testament to its diversity, with everything from street-side ramen stalls to Michelin-starred restaurants.
Tokyo.JP:
東京は、活気あふれる大都市であり、Fusion Residencyの旅の出発点として、参加者にとっては芸術的冒険の鮮やかな前奏パートです。この広大な都市は摩天楼とネオンの光で知られ、現代と伝統が融合した活気に満ちた場所です。世界中から集まったアーティストたちは創造的な旅に出発する前に、東京の急速なエネルギーの中を探索します。

東京は、皇居の静かな庭園から、ファッション愛好者やトレンドセッターが集う活気ある原宿の街並みまで、例えるなら万華鏡のような多彩な体験を提供します。街の料理シーンもその多様性を象徴しており、路上のラーメン屋台からミシュラン星付きレストランまで、幅広いグルメが楽しめます。

Partnerships.EN: FUSION partners with one of a kind spaces and institutions worldwide. We align with brands who explore bridging creative gaps. Our Partners/Sponsors understand the value of supporting and interpreting the arts, and developing artist on a global scale.
Partnerships.JP: FUSIONは、アートにおいての隔たりを埋めることを探求するブランドと連携し、世界中の独自でユニークな場所や機関とパートナーシップを築いています。私たちのパートナーやスポンサーは、アートを理解しサポートすることの重要性、そしてアーティストをグローバルな規模で発展させることに価値をおいています。

fusion2025.EN:
FUSION is a highly immersive, cross-cultural, and multidisciplinary experience in Japan. For our fifth installment we'll focus on the profound dialogues that artists engage in.

In the serene setting of Kaga-hyakumangoku Onsen, a traditional Japanese hot spring resort, Fusion artists will come together to create an environment where collaboration, tradition, and global contemporary practices within the arts intersect.

As we gear up for our 2025 Japan program, we are poised to deliver one of the most impactful global collaborative artists' residencies to date.
fusion2025.JP:
FUSIONは、異文化的で多分野における日本での没入体験です。第5回目となる今回は、アーティストが取り組む深い対話に焦点を当てました。

伝統的な日本の温泉リゾートである加賀百万石温泉の静かな環境の中で、Fusionアーティストたちは協力し合い、伝統とグローバルな現代美術が交差する空間を作り上げます。

2025年の日本プログラムに向けて、私たちはこれまでで最もインパクトのある国際的な共同アーティスト・レジデンシーを実現しようとしています。

fusionTokyo2026.EN:
FUSION is a highly immersive, cross-cultural, and multidisciplinary artist residency based in Japan. Now in its sixth edition, we’re reshaping how artists live, work, and grow in today’s creative landscape.

Set in the historic heart of Nihonbashi, Tokyo—where centuries-old merchant culture meets cutting-edge innovation—Fusion artists will gather in a district that embodies Japan’s rich duality of heritage and modernity. Surrounded by artisanal legacy, architectural elegance, and the fast-paced rhythm of the capital, this residency becomes a living dialogue between global contemporary art and the cultural depth of urban Japan.

The BnA × Fusion program marks the launch of a bold, fast-paced artist residency model—designed to push boundaries, foster collaboration, and redefine artistic development in the modern age.
fusionTokyo2026.JP:
FUSIONは、日本を舞台にした異文化的かつ多分野にわたる没入型アーティスト・レジデンシーです。第6回目となる今回は、アーティストが現代の創造的環境の中で「暮らし」「働き」「成長する」在り方を再定義していきます。

歴史ある東京・日本橋——長い商人文化と最先端の革新が共存するこのエリアに、Fusionアーティストたちが集結します。職人の伝統、美しい建築、そして首都・東京のスピード感あふれる都市の鼓動に囲まれながら、このレジデンシーは、グローバルな現代アートと日本の都市文化との対話の場となります。

BnA × Fusionプログラムは、境界を越え、創造性を育み、現代におけるアーティストの成長を再構築する、スピード感と挑戦に満ちた新しいアーティスト・レジデンシーの幕開けを意味します。

Team.EN: Fusion's staff personifies the concept of creators guiding creators. While they may often work behind the scenes, orchestrating schedules and curating programs tailored to each artist's individual growth, they are also dynamic creators in their own right. Beyond our annual programs, you can find each member of Fusion's staff at the forefront of their respective creative professions and practices.
Team.JP: Fusionのスタッフは、クリエーターがクリエーターを導くというコンセプトを体現しています。彼らは、スケジュールを調整したり、アーティストそれぞれの成長に合わせたプログラムをキュレーションをしたり、しばしば舞台裏で活動するのと同時に彼ら自身も活力に溢れるクリエーターであります。年間プログラムに加えて、Fusionのスタッフ一人ひとりがそれぞれの創造的な専門的職業や実践の最前線で活躍しています。

akari.EN:
Akari Koizumi is a Photographer, Dancer, and Project Director. Born in Tokyo, Japan, Akari started dance training in her later teenage years and found her true passion in performance art when she traveled to the country of Jamaica.

In Jamaica, Akari created works with local street performance artists, along with documenting performance artists of the 'Flexn' community in Brooklyn. Flexn, a modern Brooklyn-born dance style with an exceptional sense and expression of emotion, deeply influenced Akari's interest in performance arts.

Akari has covered several projects in multiple countries. One of such projects, called 'local x local,' combined traditional local dance forms from different cultures, history, and countries in a documentary-style film. Akari also photographs for global brands, with a focus on collaboration with dancer performances to develop cutting-edge global marketing campaigns. Akari lived in Brooklyn, N.Y., from 2010 to 2020.
akari.JP:
Akari Koizumiは、フォトグラファー、ダンサー、そしてプロジェクトディレクターです。東京で生まれ、十代後半からダンスを始め、ジャマイカを訪れた際にパフォーマンスアートへの真の情熱を見出しました。

ジャマイカでは地元のストリートパフォーマンスアーティストと作品を作り、ニューヨーク・ブルックリンの「Flexn」コミュニティのパフォーマンスアーティストの記録もしてきました。ブルックリン発祥のモダンダンススタイルであるFlexnは、感情豊かな表現が特徴で、Akariのパフォーマンスアートへの関心に大きな影響を与えました。

彼女は複数の国で様々なプロジェクトを手掛けてきた経験があり、その一つである「local x local」プロジェクトは、異なる文化、歴史、国の伝統的なダンス形式を組み合わせたドキュメンタリースタイルの映像作品です。また、グローバルなブランドの撮影なども行い、ダンスパフォーマンスとのコラボレーションを通じて、最先端のグローバルマーケティングキャンペーンを発展させてきました。2010年から2020年までニューヨークのブルックリン在住。

ameer.EN:
Ameer Carter is a multidisciplinary designer whose work spans policy, visual journalism, sustainable fashion, social design, manufacturing, and the evolving landscape of blockchain technology. A pioneer in cryptomedia, he explores how digital media—art, music, writing—gains new dimensions of ownership and provenance through blockchain.

His role at Fusion as Marketing and Digital Partnerships Director leverages his expertise in Web3 and art markets to promote the residency, drive strategic partnerships, and amplify Fusion’s presence across traditional and digital media. Ameer's innovative approach fuels the platform's growth and fosters collaborative creativity.
ameer.JP:
Ameer Carterは、政策、ビジュアルジャーナリズム、サステナブルファッション、社会的デザイン、製造、そして進化するブロックチェーンテクノロジー領域においての多分野にわたるデザイナーです。彼はクリプトメディアの先駆者としてブロックチェーンを通して、デジタルメディア—アート、音楽、ライティング—の所有権と起源の新しい次元を獲得する方法を探求しています。

彼の役割は、マーケティングおよびデジタルパートナーシップディレクターとして、Web3やアートマーケットの専門知識を活かし、レジデンシーを促進し、戦略的パートナーシップを推進し、Fusionの存在感を従来のメディアとデジタルメディアの双方において高めることです。Ameerの革新的なアプローチはプラットフォームの成長を促進し、共同の創造性を育んでいます。

brian.EN:
Brian Felix, a Creative Director and contemporary artist, beautifully fuses his passion for the moving image and visual storytelling. With a foundation in Automotive Engineering and Film Studies, Brian blends a technical approach with artistic vision. He draws upon his cross-disciplinary expertise to delve into the nuances of media synthesis, video art, and generative art, unraveling the comical social cues and agreed-upon banalities of our society.

Brian has directed the raw and evocative ‘Spiteful’ music video for IX Wulf, capturing the song's essence with a minimalist approach. He also contributed as a photographer for ‘Bears Discover Fire,’ an adaptation of Terry Bisson's award-winning short story, adding a unique dimension to the film's storytelling. His dedication to the arts is further exemplified by his previous role as Creative Director at Fameless Quarterly, a platform championing underrepresented artists.

Through his dedication to continuous learning and his cross-disciplinary mindset, Brian Felix is pioneering the seamless integration of art and technology, redefining the landscape of contemporary art.
brian.JP:
ブライアン・フェリックスは、クリエイティブディレクター、そして現代アーティストとして映像とビジュアルストーリーテリングへの情熱を見事に融合させています。自動車工学とフィルムスタディの基盤を持つ彼は、技術的アプローチと芸術的ビジョンを組み合わせています。学際的な専門知識を活かし、メディア合成、ビデオアート、生成アートのニュアンスに深く迫り、私たちの社会における滑稽な社会的合図や共通の陳腐さを解き明かしています。

ブライアンは、IX Wulfの音楽ビデオ「Spiteful」を監督し、その本質をミニマリストなアプローチで捉えました。また、テリー・ビソンの受賞歴のある短編小説を原作とした映画「Bears Discover Fire」において写真家としても貢献し、映画のストーリーテリングに独自の次元を加えました。彼の芸術への献身は、代表的なアーティストを支援するプラットフォームであるFameless Quarterlyでクリエイティブディレクターを務めたことによってさらに実証されています。

Brian Felixは、継続的な学びへの献身と異分野間的なマインドセットを通じて、アートとテクノロジーの調和した統合を先駆け、現代アートの風景を再定義しています。

hiroyuki.EN:
Hiroyuki Yorozuya is a driving force in the success of the Fusion Artist Residency in Kaga City, Ishikawa, Japan. In 2017, Yorozuya played a pivotal role in helping the Fusion team establish its first global residency at Hatori Onsen, bringing his expertise and the support of the Hatori Onsen staff to ensure a seamless experience for 24 international artists. Since then, he has worked closely with Fusion, demonstrating a deep commitment to nurturing artists across all disciplines. His dedication to fostering creativity and his deep connections within Kaga City have been essential in making each residency impactful for both the local community and visiting artists.

After years of successful collaboration, Yorozuya now serves as an advisor to Fusion, guiding the team with his vision of showcasing the majestic beauty and artisanal culture of Kaga City to the world.
hiroyuki.JP: 萬谷浩幸は、日本の石川県加賀市にあるFusionアーティストレジデンスの成功を支える原動力です。2017年、葉渡莉温泉での最初のグローバルレジデンスを確立する際、温泉スタッフによる支援と専門知識を提供し、24名の国際的なアーティストがスムーズで最適な体験をするための重要な役割を果たしました。それ以来彼はFusionと密接に協力し合い、すべての分野のアーティストの育成に取り組むことを深く決意し実行しています。 彼の創造性を育むことに対しての献身的な姿勢と、自らがもつ加賀市内での深いつながりは、レジデンシープログラムが訪れるアーティストと加賀市コミュニティの両方にとって影響力のあるものとなるために必要不可欠な要素です。 数年に渡る成果を納めた協力体制の後、萬谷浩幸は現在、Fusionのアドバイザーとして、加賀市の壮大な美しさと職人文化を世界に紹介するというビジョンを持ってチームを指導しています。

starr.EN:
Starnilas Oge is a multidisciplinary designer with a profound passion for Men's Fashion, programming, game design, world-building, music, and the arts as a whole.

His creative and entrepreneurial endeavors extend from developing a fashion tech label, to developing the Fusion platform and programs, to collaborating with artists and companies in crafting compelling brands and campaigns

As the director of the FUSION platform and residency, Starr takes the helm in orchestrating and coordinating the creative and logistical components essential for blending culture, art, and collaboration at an international scale.
starr.JP:
スターニラス・オジは、メンズファッション、プログラミング、ゲームデザイン、ワールドビルディング、音楽、そして芸術全般に深いパッションを持つマルチ分野のデザイナーです。

ファッションテックブランドの開発から、Fusionプラットフォームやプログラムの構築、そしてアーティストや企業とのコラボレーションを通じて魅力的なブランドやキャンペーンを作り上げることまで、彼のクリエイティブで起業家的な取り組みは多岐にわたります。

FUSIONプラットフォームとレジデンシーのディレクターとして、スターは文化、芸術、そしてコラボレーションを国際的な規模で融合させるために必要な、クリエイティブおよびロジスティックな要素を指揮し調整する役割を担っています。

zoia.EN:
Zoia Amadi is an architectural designer with experience in various design typologies and has a strong passion for cultural and vernacular influences in design. With an unique academic background, including degrees in both architecture and interior design, she has honed a keen understanding of the intricacies of the built environment while incorporating strong influence from art and film.

Over the years, Zoia has carved a distinguished career in the form of several built projects. From residential spaces that exude comfort and elegance to commercial projects that balance functionality and aesthetics, she has left an indelible mark on each project.

Drawing from a profound respect for regional heritage, she crafts designs that seamlessly integrate with the surroundings, paying homage to local traditions. and continually seeks inspiration from historical sites and local architectural treasures.

With this unique blend of academic expertise, cross-disciplinary experience, and a deep respect for cultural context, Zoia continues to shape diverse environments with designs that honor the essence of each typology.
zoia.JP:
Zoiz Amadiは、さまざまなデザインタイポロジーの経験を持つ建築デザイナーであり、デザインにおける文化的および伝統的な影響に強い情熱を抱いています。彼女は建築とインテリアデザインの両方の学位を持ち、アートや映画から大きな影響を受けながら、建築環境の複雑さを理解する鋭い感覚を磨いてきました。

長年にわたり、Zoiaは数々の建築プロジェクトを通じて卓越したキャリアを築いてきました。快適さとエレガンスを兼ね備えた住宅空間から、機能性と美しさを両立させた商業プロジェクトまで、彼女は各プロジェクトにおいて不朽の痕跡を残しています。

地域の遺産に対する深い敬意を基に、Zoiaは周囲と調和しながら地元の伝統に敬意を表するデザインを生み出しています。彼女は常に歴史的な場所や地元の貴重な建築遺産からインスピレーションを得ています。

このような学問的専門知識、学際的な経験、そして文化的文脈への深い敬意を融合させたアプローチによりZoiaは、各デザインチポロジーの本質を尊重したデザインで、多様な環境を形作り続けています。

hundred.EN:
Fusion 100 is a new global art fair launching Fall 2026 within a serene, traditional Japanese onsen in Kaga City, Ishikawa, Japan. We're redefining the presentation and collection of utilitarian art and antiquities.

We look forward to gathering passionate patrons from around the world.
hundred.JP:
Fusion 100は、2026年秋に石川県加賀市の穏やかで伝統的な温泉街で開催される、新しいグローバルアートフェアです。私たちは、実用芸術や古美術品の展示と収集の新しい形を提案しています。

世界中の情熱的な支援者の皆様との出会いを楽しみにしています。

eiheiji.text: The Fusion Residency culminates with a visit to Eiheiji Temple, a well-known Zen Buddhist temple. This serene sanctuary, nestled amidst lush forests, encourages contemplation and meditation. The temple's architecture and surroundings evoke a sense of timelessness, offering a profound opportunity for reflection and inspiration.

journey.text: The Fusion Residency's journey through Tokyo, Kaga, Kanazawa, Komatsu, and Eiheiji is a dynamic exploration of Japan's contrasting facets, from the energetic urban pulse of Tokyo to the tranquil and culturally rich landscapes of Ishikawa. Each location holds its unique allure, shaping the artists' experiences and fostering transformation and creativity throughout their residency. The journey, like the Shinkansen ride, is a transition from one world to another, leaving participants with lasting memories and inspiration drawn from the tapestry of Japan's art, culture, and tradition.

kaga.text: Kaga, the heart of the Fusion Residency experience, welcomes artists with open arms. This city is renowned for its onsen (hot springs) culture, which provides a unique opportunity for relaxation and reflection. Artists settle into traditional Japanese accommodations with tatami-matted rooms, immersing themselves in the local culture. Kaga's streets are adorned with artisanal shops, reflecting its rich tradition of craftsmanship.

kanazawa.text:
Kanazawa, a neighboring city to Kaga, is home to the 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, making it a hub for artistic inspiration. This city, often referred to as 'Little Kyoto' due to its preserved Edo-era architecture and well-maintained geisha districts, beckons with its rich cultural heritage. Artists explore its gardens, including the renowned Kenrokuen Garden, a masterpiece of Japanese landscaping.

The city's craft traditions thrive, with gold leaf production being a notable specialty. Visiting workshops and galleries provides a glimpse into these time-honored crafts. The fusion of tradition and innovation in Kanazawa mirrors the artistic journey itself.

shinkansen.text: The Shinkansen, Japan's iconic high-speed train system, becomes the conduit for transitioning from Tokyo's urban hustle to the rural landscapes of Ishikawa. The sleek, futuristic trains whisk passengers away at incredible speeds, affording them breathtaking views of Japan's changing scenery. This journey is not just about distance but also a transition from the urban chaos to the tranquility of the countryside, setting the stage for the artistic exploration that awaits.

tokyo.text:
Tokyo, the bustling metropolis and the starting point of the Fusion Residency journey, serves as a vibrant prelude to the artistic adventure awaiting participants. This sprawling city, known for its skyscrapers and neon lights, is a vibrant fusion of modernity and tradition. Artists from around the world gather here, exploring Tokyo's fast-paced energy before embarking on their creative voyage.

Tokyo offers a kaleidoscope of experiences, from the serene gardens of the Imperial Palace to the lively streets of Harajuku, where fashionistas and trendsetters congregate. The city's culinary scene is a testament to its diversity, with everything from street-side ramen stalls to Michelin-starred restaurants.

Partners.bio:
Hatori Onsen, Our primary international partner located in Ishikawa, Japan, helped give birth to the first iteration of the FUSION residency.

This gorgeous resort accomodates the Fusion Japan group annually with an authentic experience in traditional Japanese Onsen(Hot Spring) hospitalty and culture.

Deeply connected to their local community in the town of Kaga-City, Hatori Onsen helps break down cultural barriers through assited planning and promotions of our open workshops, special performances and exhibition.
Partners.name: Hatori Onsen

Partners.bio:
Our latest partner, BnA_WALL, located in the historic Nihonbashi district of Tokyo, joins us in launching a bold and immersive chapter of the FUSION residency program. As Tokyo’s newest creative epicenter—with an art hotel, rotating mural project, and artist studio—BnA_WALL brings energy, innovation, and a strong community-driven ethos to the heart of our residency experience.

Together, we present ‘BnA Fusion’, a dynamic program that invites artists to live, create, and exchange ideas in a space where art and hospitality merge. With 26 artist-designed rooms and an on-site café/lounge that pulses with conversation and collaboration, BnA_WALL fosters an atmosphere of continuous inspiration.

Through our partnership, we aim to cultivate cross-cultural dialogue, experimental exhibitions, and vibrant public art experiences—redefining what it means to create and connect in Tokyo.
Partners.name: BnA Wall

Partners.bio:
As a valued partner, Ideal Glass Studios, founded by Willard Morgan, brings their expertise in film and TV production to our collaboration. They have a rich history of nurturing artistic expression and fostering dialogue.

With their commitment to open and clear communication, Ideal Glass Studios aligns seamlessly with Fusion's mission to inspire profound conversations in the world of art. Together, we celebrate diversity and creativity without bounds.
Partners.name: Ideal Glass Studios

Partners.address: 7 Chome-10-5 Nishishinjuku, Shinjuku City, Tokyo 160-0023, Japan
Partners.bio:
Located in the dynamic district of Shinjuku, WPÜ SHINJUKU is more than just a space—it’s a thriving ecosystem designed for creatives, travelers, and cultural explorers. With its multifaceted offerings—including a hotel, student residence, café, craft beer diner, gallery, and radio station—WPÜ serves as a platform for meaningful exchange and creative expression.

As our newest partner and the official home for the Tokyo leg of the Fusion Residency, WPÜ SHINJUKU offers an unparalleled gateway into the city’s artistic and cultural pulse. Together, we aim to build an environment where global artists and local communities intersect, collaborate, and grow. WPÜ’s commitment to cultivating an ever-evolving creative landscape makes them an ideal partner in redefining what artistic residencies can be in Japan
Partners.name: WPU

Partners.bio:
Twin City is a global home swapping community designed for millennials, making travel more affordable by eliminating accommodation costs. By enabling seamless home exchanges, building meaningful connections, and offering authentic travel experiences, Twin City redefines the way people explore the world.

fusion2017.desc:
FUSION 2017 marked the inception of our voyage into Kaga City, Japan, a project born from the collaborative vision of a creative collective consisting of up to 30 artists hailing from New York City and Tokyo. It all began with a multidisciplinary exhibition in Tokyo, Japan, where this diverse group of talents came together to create art that transcended boundaries.

From this initial concept, FUSION 2017 evolved to embrace artists from the United States, Brazil, and Poland, expanding its reach and horizons. Driven by ambitious goals and a profound appreciation for the craftsmanship of local artisans, the FUSION 17 cohort became the bedrock upon which the Fusion residencies were built, fostering enduring relationships that transcended borders and cultures. These connections, nurtured through the collaborative spirit of art, continue to thrive and inspire, reflecting the lasting impact of this creative journey.

fusion2018.desc:
After our inaugural residency, the FUSION 2018 cohort embarked on a more intimate journey, crafting a novel program that focused on building closer connections among artists. This immersive experience involved meeting local artisans and business owners at their workplaces, fostering an environment of mutual learning and the exchange of artistic practices.

Hatori Onsen and the Kaga City community in Ishikawa , Japan once again opened its doors to us, welcoming our return for a profound exploration of the region's unique and traditional creative techniques. This deep dive into the heart of Kaga City allowed us to uncover and embrace the rich artistic heritage that defines the area, further strengthening our ties to the local community and its invaluable artistic wisdom.
fusion2018.title: FUSION 2018

fusion2019.desc:
Building upon the achievements of our prior programs, Fusion 19 scaled up its collaboration efforts and embraced a wider spectrum of multidisciplinary expression. The enthusiastic support of Hatori Onsen and the Kaga City community and neighboring artisans played a pivotal role in this growth.

Our artists took center stage at the KagaFest Music Festival, sharing their creations with the broader Japanese creative community. Simultaneously, they embarked on journeys to explore traditional, almost forgotten towns undergoing revitalization processes. These experiences led to deep collaborations with local entities that resonated with our shared vision.

This journey culminated in yet another triumphant group exhibition, accompanied by an extended showcase of the artworks created during the residency. This showcase found a home through our Tokyo partner, Think Green Produce Inc., at the Mustard Hotel in Asakusa, Tokyo. This strategic extension allowed our artists' work to reach a broader audience and further solidified Fusion 19 as a successful celebration of creativity, community, and cross-cultural connections.

8-21.description:
The Kitamaebune (literally “northern-bound ships”) were merchant vessels that sailed along the Sea of Japan during the Edo (1603–1868) and Meiji (1868–1912) periods. These ships played a vital role in connecting Japan’s western and northern regions, transporting goods, culture, and information from Osaka to Hokkaido and back.
Following seasonal winds and currents, Kitamaebune traveled a long route that included ports in present-day Kyoto, Fukui, Ishikawa, Niigata, Akita, and beyond. They carried rice, sake, soy sauce, seaweed, herring, and local specialties, contributing to regional economies and fostering cultural exchange.
More than just trade ships, Kitamaebune helped shape the lifestyles, architecture, and culinary traditions of port towns across the Japan Sea coast. Many of these towns still preserve historic merchant houses, warehouses, and festivals that celebrate their maritime heritage.

fusion2025.faq:
Q: How long has Fusion been around?
A: Fusion has been around since 2017.

Q: What is expected from the artist?
A: Artists are expected to exhibit their developing or completed work and participate in a podcast interview.

Q: What type of organization is Fusion?
A: Fusion is a private, for proit organization spearheaded by designer Starnilas Oge as an annual project, alongside a talented group of creative entrepreneurs

Q: Duration of residency:
A: The residency duration is 3 weeks.

Q: Accommodation type:
A: Artists stay in shared traditional Japanese loft rooms.

Q: Are there additional costs?
A: No, there are no hidden fees beyond what is listed in the details section. However, during the FUSION residency, artists may have the opportunity to participate in optional events organized by local artisans and business owners. These events are often spontaneous and may include hidden beach concerts or specialized group dinners. It's a good idea to consider these random opportunities that could arise.

Q: What should I bring?
A: Bring your art supplies, casual clothing, hiking/outdoor wear, and special event attire.

Q: Can I visit other prefectures on my own?
A: Yes, artists are free to explore neighboring cities during the residency. While artists have taken day trips away from the group in the past, our primary goal is to facilitate diverse dialogues, interactions, and collaborations between artists and the local community. We encourage artists interested in the complete experience to join. If you're primarily interested in visiting Japan, consider joining as a Guest.

Q: Can I bring a friend or family member?
A: Friends and family can join as Fusion guests, but guest slots are limited. Please inquire for additional information.

Q: Do I need a Visa?
A: U.S. Citizens are allowed to stay in Japan for up to 90 days. For participants traveling from other countries, please visit https://jp.usembassy.gov/ and select your country of residence for more details.

Q: Can I purchase my own flights?
A: Yes, selected participants who wish to purchase their own roundtrip flight tickets receive a maximum $800 credit towards their participation fee.

Q: Application:
A: Submit examples of your work to info@FusionArt.World to start a conversation. Our selection process is based on your ongoing development, promotion of your art, your goals and ambition, and your story. Artists from all over the world are encouraged to apply.

Q: Group:
A: Typical Fusion programs consist of 24 artists from various disciplines, including painters, sculptors, musicians, dancers, and more.

Q: Experience:
A: The Fusion experience includes creative activities in Tokyo, exploring Japan's natural beauty, meeting local artists, completing artwork for an exhibition, and visiting serene Japanese temples, among other activities.

Q: What is Twin City Global?
A: Twin City Global is a home swap network that allows artists to exchange their homes with other artists around the world. This service is available to all Fusion participants. For more information, visit https://www.twincityglobal.com/

Starnilas Oge is a multidisciplinary designer with a profound passion for Men's Fashion, programming, game design, world-building, music, and the arts as a whole.

His creative and entrepreneurial endeavors extend from developing a fashion tech label, to developing the Fusion platform and programs, to collaborating with artists and companies in crafting compelling brands and campaigns.

Team.bio:
Akari Koizumi is a Photographer, Dancer, and Project Director. Born in Tokyo, Japan, Akari started dance training in her later teenage years and found her true passion in performance art when she traveled to the country of Jamaica. In Jamaica, Akari created works with local street performance artists, along with documenting performance artists of the 'Flexn' community in Brooklyn. Flexn, a modern Brooklyn-born dance style with an exceptional sense and expression of emotion, deeply influenced Akari's interest in performance arts.

Akari has covered several projects in multiple countries. One of such projects, called 'local x local,' combined traditional local dance forms from different cultures, history, and countries in a documentary-style film. Akari also photographs for global brands, with a focus on collaboration with dancer performances to develop cutting-edge global marketing campaigns. Akari lived in Brooklyn, N.Y., from 2010 to 2020.

Team.bio:
Zoia Amadi is an architectural designer with experience in various design typologies and has a strong passion for cultural and vernacular influences in design. With an unique academic background, including degrees in both architecture and interior design, she has honed a keen understanding of the intricacies of the built environment while incorporating strong influence from art and film.

Over the years, Zoia has carved a distinguished career in the form of several built projects. From residential spaces that exude comfort and elegance to commercial projects that balance functionality and aesthetics, she has left an indelible mark on each project.

Drawing from a profound respect for regional heritage, she crafts designs that seamlessly integrate with the surroundings, paying homage to local traditions. and continually seeks inspiration from historical sites and local architectural treasures.

With this unique blend of academic expertise, cross-disciplinary experience, and a deep respect for cultural context, Zoia continues to shape diverse environments with designs that honor the essence of each typology.

Hiroyuki Yorozuya is a driving force behind the success of the Fusion Artist Residency in Kaga City, Ishikawa, Japan. In 2017, Yorozuya played a pivotal role in helping the Fusion team establish its first global residency at Hatori Onsen, bringing his expertise and the support of the Hatori Onsen staff to ensure a seamless experience for 24 international artists. Since then, he has worked closely with Fusion, demonstrating a deep commitment to nurturing artists across all disciplines. His dedication to fostering creativity and his deep connections within Kaga City have been essential in making each residency impactful for both the local community and visiting artists.

After years of successful collaboration, Yorozuya now serves as an advisor to Fusion, guiding the team with his vision of showcasing the majestic beauty and artisanal culture of Kaga City to the world.

I’m a painter currently living in Los Angeles, California.  I'm a full-time studio artist, producing work for a variety of clients in education, food, tech, and more.  I also travel to produce large-scale public murals around the world.  

My personal art style is defined by technique in application and dynamic color, and is blocky, pixellated, and bright. My work usually represents animals, human features, or objects up close, broken down into interpretations of light and color. My paintings are designed to exist carefully between mechanical and fluid, representational and abstracted.

4NWheAHthiRnUERfVdT9FDH3S3u2.bio:
Eve V Eggleston is a working artist, educator, and LMT living in Portland, Oregon. Eggleston earned a dual Bachelors of Science degrees in Studio Fine Arts and Psychology from the University of Indianapolis; and later returned to her alma-mater, earning a MA in Social Practice Art in 2019.  Blossoming from the artistic relationships forged during this graduate work, Eve worked as the beekeeper in residence and part-time event staff at Tube Factory Artspace for BigCar Collaborative. This connection to Big Car Media further blossomed in 2020 when Eve co-curated a series of in person and virtual events with Eduardo Luna as a part of the 10 East Arts 2020 Summer Fellowship.
Starting during the world’s quarantine, from 2020 through 2022 Eve instructed Beginning Drawing courses at Ivy Tech Community College in an adjunct capacity, focusing on fundamentals, still life drawing, and figure drawing with live models.  This materialized in a growing fascination for studying realistic drawing and painting; a humanitarian endeavor in an ever-growing digital AI world. Noticing a lack of public spaces to work with models outside of academia, Eggleston created the Indianapolis Figure Guild through the Indiana Arts Commission's 2021-2022 On-Ramp Fellowship.   Eggleston has since taught Ethics and Massage Clinic during 2024 and 2025 at East West College of the Healing Arts in downtown Portland, and is currently enrolled at Point of View Tattoo School.  Most recently in July 2025 Eve co-facilitated, alongside Joanne Kollman, a charcoal figure drawing workshop led by guest artist and educator Henry Yan at the Oregon Society of Artists. 
Since moving to Portland Oregon, Eve’s need to improve and explore has only multiplied; from traveling to rural France with the Chateaux Orquevaux artist residency in 2023, to an island off of Spain to attend Quarantine Events during their 2024 Interzone residency; and now with unbridled joy in 2025 going to Japan to participate in the FUSION artist residency. 

www.eveveggleston.com

5ViLev6khafiN3alRkoubtivKCf2.bio: Jah’Nyah Spencer is a Lynn, Massachusetts based illustrator, muralist and creative director, with a strong focus in eccentric portraiture and character design. Currently a full-time student at Lesley University, Spencer’s creative practice is rooted in affirming the identities of marginalized youth, helping them step into their power through representation, storytelling, and self exploration. Her murals often depict empowering stories resembling a shot from an animated show, creating movement, and leaving viewers eager to see what’ll happen next.  Dedicated to bridging gaps in communities, Spencer also works part-time as the Creative Engagement Producer at the Lynn Museum & Art Center, where she directs Final Fridays: an ongoing programming initiative dedicated to empowering the next generation of artists and creatives, actively shaping the arts infrastructure in the city of Lynn, MA.

5rhOuM26ptOHH6HYJYDBRxE6AtB3.bio:
I am a Japanese-Korean American writer working on my debut novel, a dystopian narrative set in a future where literature and creative thought are endangered. With the mentorship of award-winning novelist Ernesto Mestre, this work is both a protest and a love letter—to the written word, to resistance, and to identity reclaimed.

Growing up in the United States with a Japanese father and Korean mother, I inherited fragmented versions of their cultures. I often felt like a ghost in both—visible, but not fully seen. When I visited Korea last year with my mother, I felt something begin to reconfigure in my self-understanding. Japan, however, is more complicated. My relationship with my father is strained, and when I distanced myself from him, I unknowingly distanced myself from the culture that shaped him. 

Returning to Japan last year on my own terms, I began to reclaim that part of myself, not as his daughter, but as a woman, a writer, and an artist.

5yxh1dhRYHQawQ7NhjRPAArKJUG2.bio: Ren is a photographer, streetwear designer, essayist, and producer/songwriter. She is an avid traveler and her brand Common Skies was inspired by the joy and color of the places she visits. As a photographer, Ren invites you to get to know the subject more intimately, whether a person or place. What has this person done and seen? What has happened here? Her work aims to create inclusive spaces and encourage discovery, eschewing virality for authenticity.

641plqOHW8hwJ1172OJh0k8sM3B3.bio:
Suwichada is a Thai American artist based in Joshua Tree, California.  She is an interdisciplinary artist who begins by recalling her memories in writings and transfers them into paintings, sculpture and performance.

"My art practice is focused on expressing the relationship between ourselves and the natural world.   I believe the disconnect between our basic primitive human state and today’s refined human condition is causing unconscious melancholy. 
 I construct a visual and emotional space where axiological narratives of pain and beauty intersect.  Translating my experiences and emotions into an immersive visual form helping viewers better understand themselves and the world around them."

66NQa5LcL8cHsEZOUERV1P8j9cE2.bio: George F. Baker III is an Atlanta-based Muralist, Illustrator, and Public Speaker who infuses a child-like joy into all of his creative endeavors. Over the course of 6 years practicing muralism, he has painted over 50 murals across the United States (as well as a couple in London) and has produced numerous illustrations. Regardless of the medium, he is always eager to offer encouragement to individuals, urging them to embrace their inner-child more in their daily lives. He firmly believes that by doing so, people become the most authentic versions of themselves.

F3Uph6Rkrtf8eFNUnMjZEcs3V092.bio: Jess Fendo is a Detroit-based artist and designer whose work bridges brand design and large-scale murals. Her paintings focus on the depth of human experience and emotion, translating raw feeling into bold visual narratives. Whether developing design systems for major brands or bringing color to Detroit’s walls, Jess creates work that connects people through shared stories and vibrant expression.

I8d4gju2hIhp8P9YMvWchA3SjOJ2.bio: Hannah Driscoll is a Japanese American artist based in Dallas, Texas, whose work explores themes of silent separation and the tension of public spaces. Hannah’s practice is deeply inspired by Japanese and American culture and the complex nuances surrounding isolation and observation.

IU5w3nyVu4NG5i5DJthWgv6smLW2.bio:
Vic Martinez, aka FutureVic, has been in PHX punk bands since '94.
Gone Solo, he's now recording and releasing sonic slices of life and its struggles, while offering up hopeful and empowering perspectives in the wake.
Upbeat and with a surf/skate punk inspired style, his songs drop Old-School knowledge using Nu-Skool hooks.
Working album title: Apostate Perorate Resonator

J0OVbSfpKsf7zoVL4DoTCNEJbA12.bio:
Starnilas Oge is a multidisciplinary designer with a profound passion for Men's Fashion, programming, game design, world-building, music, and the arts as a whole.

His creative and entrepreneurial endeavors extend from developing a fashion tech label, to developing the Fusion platform and programs, to collaborating with artists and companies in crafting compelling brands and campaigns.

As the director of the FUSION platform and residency, Starr takes the helm in orchestrating and coordinating the creative and logistical components essential for blending culture, art, and collaboration at an international scale.

JmzOOoa0OOS9ctALZoIsQ1a7VIr2.bio: el JNGL (Jose Andres Carmiol), from Limon, Costa Rica, has evolved from a naturally talented youth into a versatile post-modern artist, influenced by a blend of graffiti, fine art, and tattooing traditions. His work, reflecting a wide range of styles and mediums, showcases a journey through personal and musical inspirations. With over fifteen years in tattooing and contributions to international art scenes, he now seeks new opportunities in South Florida, aiming to share his dynamic artistry with a broader audience.

LVWp3WbI45gptFzEvl5xAsRXu4S2.bio:
Akari Koizumi is a Photographer, Dancer, and Project Director. Born in Tokyo, Japan, Akari started dance training in her later teenage years and found her true passion in performance art when she traveled to the country of Jamaica. In Jamaica, Akari created works with local street performance artists, along with documenting performance artists of the 'Flexn' community in Brooklyn. Flexn, a modern Brooklyn-born dance style with an exceptional sense and expression of emotion, deeply influenced Akari's interest in performance arts.

Akari has covered several projects in multiple countries. One of such projects, called 'local x local,' combined traditional local dance forms from different cultures, history, and countries in a documentary-style film. Akari also photographs for global brands, with a focus on collaboration with dancer performances to develop cutting-edge global marketing campaigns. Akari lived in Brooklyn, N.Y., from 2010 to 2020.

MaW6MobSmPgVCiyJ9Wak6Rlgh933.bio: Maltese Holder is a technical designer and engineer with a background in Public Architecture, who explores the human experience through film photography and life drawing. Inspired by candid moments, Maltese’s street photography captures unguarded glimpses of people and the often-overlooked details of daily life, using the tactile nature of analog cameras to slow down and embrace patience. Their life drawings take a complementary approach, focusing on fleeting emotions and subtleties that photography might miss, creating a body of work that celebrates the raw and unfiltered essence of humanity.

NcQZIhETQSQNbFMZ9nFTyQIiGFo1.bio: Anthony R. Manzo is a graphic designer known for his innovative approach to visual arts. He gained recognition for printing small images on a large scale, effectively transforming everyday visuals into impactful statements. His work was featured in the 2006 "Art in Odd Places" festival in New York City, an event that showcases art in unconventional public spaces. Manzo's work often challenges traditional perceptions of scale and context, inviting viewers to engage with familiar images in new and thought-provoking ways.

R3C8gRUJAGZunclWKmG3B3KkyLr2.bio:
Louisiana born and Texas raised, Austin Wafer's work spans across 
various different mediums. This includes painting, writing, and 
illustration, graphic design and 3D modeling. By not limiting himself to 
one form of expression, he's seen his imagination grow to new heights, 
and insists on transporting his audience into a new world filled with 
questions on the human experience.  
From his sporadically colorful paintings, to his diverse, yet mindful 
writing and welcoming illustrations, Austin strives to present original 
work that inspires his audience to create, think, question, and imagine 
the unimaginable.

UD85EKqWGZQZpLifscwD2YSqIxm1.bio: Zac Foster is a dynamic artist whose expertise lies in transforming concepts into accessible and impactful visual narratives. With a focus on composition, craftsmanship, and execution, Zac’s work is both readable and deeply resonant, connecting audiences to his artistic vision. His distinctive illustrative style is malleable, fluid, and uniquely customizable, allowing him to create works that captivate and engage target audiences by drawing them into his intricate designs and compelling compositions.

Ve28SsWZOFVetnoIV3AFKhysX313.bio: Alfonso Abraham Cervera is a first-generation Queer Mexican American performer, educator, curator, and artivist. Currently a professor at The Ohio State University, Alfonso’s work bridges Queerness, Ballet Folklorico, and Afro-Latine social dances through a contemporary autobiographical practice known as Poc-Chuc. This inclusive technique has been celebrated for its ability to connect “the sociality of the audience with the isolated frigidity of the concert stage...resulting in a world of untethered Mexican modernity” (Enrique Manuel). In addition to his artistic pursuits, Alfonso is a certified yoga teacher, reiki healer, co-director of the non-profit Show Box L.A., and a founding member of the Primera Generación Dance Collective.

YHJNzNbH0Mb5J1sV8JgPX3JkduQ2.bio:
DJ-Laoshi [dee-jay lao-sih] is a multidisciplinary artist who currently lives and works in South Florida. Through mixed media and techniques drawn from diverse realms of visual arts and textiles, she create immersive and interactive experiences that engage, inspire and spark meaningful conversations that resonate across boundaries.
Her art collections spans various themes, from explorations of social and political issues to personal and intimate journeys that touch on eroticism. These works reflect her love for comic books, politics, current events, and the arts. Her academic pursuits and multicultural upbringing shaped by life in Jamaica, the United States, and the United Kingdom greatly shape the methodology for the approach behind the work.
From 2013 to present, she has had exhibitions in no particular order – Northern Iraq, USA, Switzerland, Italy, Spain, Germany, Japan, Grenada, France and Australia. DJ-Laoshi has been published in various newspapers and comic anthologies between Colombia, Jamaica, China, Australia and the USA over the last 20 years.

Yx4JxN3FmEZKGj7989uYfHbCr012.bio: Rodolfo Rueda is a Peruvian multidisciplinary artist whose work thrives on the unconventional and the unexpected. With a childlike approach to storytelling and an insatiable curiosity for exploring new concepts, Rodolfo’s art defies categorization, constantly morphing between nuanced subtlety and chaotic intricacies. From soft, detailed sonic landscapes to rhythmic confusion and bold visual expressions, his craft embraces the unfamiliar, rejecting traditional academic boundaries in favor of boundless exploration.

haIyASaRqrRt2xotVwEAMBZp1Hq1.bio:
Zoia Amadi is an architectural designer with experience in various design typologies and has a strong passion for cultural and vernacular influences in design. With an unique academic background, including degrees in both architecture and interior design, she has honed a keen understanding of the intricacies of the built environment while incorporating strong influence from art and film.

Over the years, Zoia has carved a distinguished career in the form of several built projects. From residential spaces that exude comfort and elegance to commercial projects that balance functionality and aesthetics, she has left an indelible mark on each project.

Drawing from a profound respect for regional heritage, she crafts designs that seamlessly integrate with the surroundings, paying homage to local traditions. and continually seeks inspiration from historical sites and local architectural treasures.

With this unique blend of academic expertise, cross-disciplinary experience, and a deep respect for cultural context, Zoia continues to shape diverse environments with designs that honor the essence of each typology.
